text: The Hoare triple {P} C {Q}, interpreted as partial correctness, asserts:
choices: C always terminates, regardless of P
If P holds before C, then C is guaranteed to terminate
C terminates and Q holds, whenever P holds initially
If P holds before C and C terminates, then Q holds afterward
explanation: Partial correctness makes termination a hypothesis: Q is guaranteed only if C terminates, and it says nothing about whether C does. Choice 2 describes total correctness [P] C [Q], which additionally demands termination; choices 0 and 1 assert termination unconditionally.
